newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: FEATURE - Vienna bourse to get facelift for new era.
newsitem.headline: FEATURE - Vienna bourse to get facelift for new era.

text.p: Vienna's historic stock exchange will throw off more than 200 years of tradition next year when it enforces dramatic reforms aimed at ensuring its survival in an increasingly competitive financial world.
"We have instituted the most serious reforms since the bourse was founded by Empress Maria Theresa", Finance Minister Rudolf Edlinger told Reuters.
"We want to create efficient structures for the modern financial services industry."
Exactly 226 years after one of Europe's smallest bourses began trading, its ruling authority, the Council of the Vienna Stock Exchange (VSE), will be replaced by the Wiener Boerse AG.
The new company is due to start operations in 1998 and will combine all trading activities, handle data sales, technology and communications.
"Competition will become even tougher and for that we have to remove existing expensive triple structures," said Ulrich Kamp, general secretary of the VSE.
The centrepiece of the reform is to bring the cash market and the futures and options exchange (OeTOB) under one umbrella -- the forthcoming Wiener Boerse AG.
At the moment the OeTOB and the electronic trading system EQOS operate independently of the VSE, creating three layers of overhead costs.
MERGER WILL GIVE CASH, FUTURES MARKETS CLEAR STRATEGY

The OeTOB, founded in 1990 by Austria's major banks, has succeeded in building up a significant market share. But EQOS, launched last July, is still far from its target of becoming the trading platform for all listed securities in Vienna.

And both the OeTOB and the VSE have failed to achieve their aim of becoming a hub for shares in Eastern European companies. An OeTOB project to create a central clearing house fell through and recently launched futures and options on its Hungarian Traded Index and Czech Traded Index have not taken off.
The VSE's ambitions to list the most important Eastern European companies in Vienna foundered in the early 1990s as new bourses in Budapest, Prague and Warsaw started successful operations.

Kamp said the merger, which also foresees that government financing agency Oesterreichische Kontrollbank AG (OeKB) will bring in its clearing activities, would give cash and futures markets a clear strategy.
Kamp, the prospective chief executive of the new Boerse AG, forecast more competitive fees and greater efficiency.
Once integration is completed, the bourse plans to launch a campaign to market itself among investors both at home and abroad, VSE spokesman Gerhard Reidlinger said.
NEW COMPANY WILL HAVE TO OVERCOME IMAGE PROBLEMS
Critics say the new company will have to overcome VSE image problems with international investors.
"The Vienna Bourse has significant image problems among foreign investors," said Claus Raidl, chief executive of high grade steel maker Boehler whose shares are listed in the blue-chip ATX index.
"In the medium term the market will decide which European bourses survive beyond the introduction of the single European currency," he added.
The Wiener Boerse AG will kick off with a capital of 100 million schillings ($8.4 million) and will eventually be controlled by the republic, Finance Minister Edlinger said.
His ministry is prepared to give financial backing over the next five years of around 20 to 30 million schillings a year.
The Finance Ministry stands to gain handsomely from the reforms.

Once they are completed, the planned dissolution of the VSE fund will earn the Ministry net assets of around 500 million schillings including the historical stock exchange building in the centre of Vienna, market sources say. ($ = 11.88 Austrian Schillings)
